new_statements.quote: 3.3. Tone. High, mid, low, falling and rising tones were noted. Table 20 presents some roots with fairly consistent tone. High and low tones are switched in Doso, except that H does not become L after a voiced obstruent. There is also some evidence of a mid tone level. Many roots, however, are more inconsistent in their tone across varieties. [Table 20 'Tones', Moo column:] *L: L ('answer' ɡwə̀b, 'bark' pɔ̀ŋ); *H (nouns): H ('eye' nɨ́ŋ, 'front' sí, 'millstone' ɲí, 'liver' ɲí); *H (verbs): H ('eat' tə́ŋ, 'push' tɔ́k, 'hit' ɓóp, 'ask' ɓíp); *M: M? ('swallow' mí, 'thing' nɨ̄ŋ)
new_statements.citation: Norton, Russell & Nlabephee Othaniel. 2020. The Jen language cluster: a comparative analysis of wordlists. Language in Africa 1(3): 17-99. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-17-99.
new_statements.locator: sec. 3.3 'Tone', printed pp. 43-45 (PDF pp. 27-29); Table 20 'Tones' on printed p. 45 (PDF p. 29)
new_statements.check: not checked by the second reader
new_statements.relation_note: Cluster-level tone inventory statement plus a per-variety tone-correspondence table with a Moo column; breathiness 'never co-occurs with high tone' (sec. 3.4). Silent on stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The Bikwin-Jen varieties, Moo included, are transcribed with lexical tone (high, mid, low plus falling and rising contours); for Moo the correspondence table shows low and high tones retained and an uncertain mid level. Nothing anywhere in the paper on word stress or accent ('stress'/'accent' 0 hits).
new_statements.exceptions: authors 'decline to reconstruct tone for items where tone is too inconsistent' across varieties; Moo's mid tone is marked 'M?'
new_statements.identity_note: Moo [gwg] (Gomu, Karim Lamido LGA) is one of the ten Bikwin-Jen varieties with its own tone-marked 300-item column; Table 20 has a dedicated 'Moo' column between Kyak and Leelau. Flagged here not as a new discovery but because it is the only opened source that characterises tone for Moo itself and no statement is held by the project for the language.

sources.note: For Moo: nothing prosodic (only absence of breathy vowels; vowel length non-phonemic 'so far' across Bikwin-Jen). For Dza: tonal language with H, M, L and three contours, tone used lexically and grammatically; breathy vowels carry only non-high tone.
